title: Successive comparison for given normalized scalar data
statement: Let ell be prime and E -> F -> L embeddings of finite Q_ell-extensions, T a scheme, D_A,D_B,D_C abelian strict coefficient tower presentations, and R_A,R_B,R_C normalized integral reduction towers. Given ScalarData D_1,D_2,D_3 for the two embeddings and their composite [def-sp-field-scalar-normalized-data], there exists Successive D_1 D_2 D_3: ordinary and derived completed-scalar and whole-system compositors satisfy their cochain counit equations; the ordinary maps act by multiplication of tensor factors; and the whole-derived-system reduction square commutes. This does not assert the existence of any of the three scalar data. Coefficient systems and their reduction maps use [def-sp-field-scalar-system-data] and [def-sp-field-scalar-reduction-data].

source.place: paragraph (1), finite free scalar extension and reduction formula

proof.text: Check on residue classes that the composite quotient coefficient maps are the direct maps. Completed projections give the same equality integrally. Tensor associativity and insertion of one define the ordinary integral compositor; transport the levelwise tensor associators through ExactExtension.level. The transition formula gives a natural isomorphism of whole systems with precisely system_tmul. Tensor universality proves inverse equations and naturality.

Localize the exact-system compositor, using the invertible counits on all complexes. For completed coefficients use a flat-term K-flat representative; ringed scalar extension preserves it. The universal derived properties give the integral compositor and both representative equations.

On this same representative the two reduction-square composites multiply the same three factors. The ideal-quotient tower scalar associator proves equality on strict complexes using the actual normalized quotient projections. ReductionComparison.representative and strict tensor descent give the required equality on all derived objects, including roofs.
